pr_title: Fade playfield to red when player health is low
pr_body:
Closes #8095

# Summary

This PR implements the `FaillingLayer`, a player overlay component which fades the playfield to red when the player health falls under a defined threshold.
The component is avalaible as a shared component to enable its use by rulesets interested by that functionnality.

## Changes to Player

- Every child of type `HealthDisplay` in `DrawableRuleset.Overlay` will now be bound to the ruleset's HealthProcessor on player loading
## Rulesets on which this has been applied

- osu!standard
- osu!catch
- osu!mania
pr_comments: This definitely needs easing. Otherwise maps with high HP drain have major flashing during streams.
This is going to need a config setting, imo.

I've fixed the following issues:
- HUD elements should not be added at a ruleset level. They are separate layers.
- Check health processor type to avoid this, rather than local initialisation.
- Changed effect to be less full-screen.
- You made a base `HealthDisplay` method class but didn't use the new function for the standard health display's binding.
- All words in `LabelText` are included in keywords. All the keywords you specified were redundant.
- Tests shouldn't use `WaitStep` when `UntilStep` can be used. Also just tidied them up in general (too much copy paste).
- `Lerp` should be used instead of `ValueAt` for ongoing lerps.

Not sure if this needs to be a toggle, but I guess no harm for now.

@smoogipoo request re-review on this.

Applied a few more fixes:
* Removed now unnecessary bind inside `Player`.
* Safety for config bind order.

issue_context.title: Add fade to red on low-HP effect
issue_context.body:
**Describe the new feature:** 

On stable if you have shaders enabled your screen will start fading to red when your HP start getting low. This is useful to have when you like playing with no UI but still want to know what HP you are at.
comments: For the record, this was toggled using the Shaders graphics setting. It should probably still be toggled as some people (at least all of my friends) find this effect too distracting.

review_comments: This again seems to be prematurely engineered, why is this `virtual`?

This was marked virtual to allow implementors of the `HealthDisplay` class to bind to other properties of the `HealthProcessor` if they need to but I guess this can be reverted to a normal method in a lack of a current usage overriding the method.

As a general rule, make things as simple as they can be when going forward with something new. Don't try to anticipate future usages, most of the time you'll fail in trying to do so anyway. Things can be changed when they need to be changed.
Public fields are sort of eh for me. Would just rather have it a property but it's not anything major.
Yeah, it should have stayed an auto-prop but CI inspection complains about it being convertible to an get-only auto-prop so I made it a field to make CI stop complaining about it..
